meta.description: Defines how our wgpu-py base API differs from the web-api (the one derived from webgpu.idl).
meta.notes: We mostly *remove* things that we cannot replicate on desktop. So that we get an API surface that is the intersection of what we can use on desktop and web.

enumerate_adapters_async.doc: Get a list of adapter objects available on the current system.

enumerate_adapters_sync.doc: Get a list of adapter objects available on the current system.

get_canvas_context.doc:
Get the GPUCanvasContext object for the appropriate backend.

Note that the recommended way to get a context is to instead use the ``rendercanvas`` library.

The ``present_info`` dict should have a ``window`` field containing the window id. On Linux there should also be ``platform`` field to distinguish between 'wayland' and 'x11', and a ``display`` field for the display id. For the Pyodide backend, the ``window`` is the ``<canvas>`` object. This dict is an interface between `rendercanvas`` and ``wgpu-py``.

physical_size.doc: Get the physical size of the current framebuffer.

set_physical_size.doc: Set the current framebuffer physical size.

width.doc: The new width of the framebuffer.

height.doc: The new height of the framebuffer.

get_preferred_format.doc: Get the preferred surface texture format.

present.doc: Present what has been drawn to the current texture, by compositing it to the canvas.

uid.doc:
A unique id (integer) for this object.

The value is unique to the process; in contrast to ``id(ob)``, the numbers are never reused.

summary.doc: A one-line summary of the info of this adapter (device, adapter_type, backend_type).

adapter.doc: The adapter object corresponding to this device.
